content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To win the channel nine pizza contest, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Assemble the final competition pizza (10 minutes)
Step 2. Print out the official entry forms (5 minutes)
Step 3. Prepare the secret tomato sauce base (1 hour)
Step 4. Proof the pizza dough in a warm environment (2 hours)
Step 5. Slice high-moisture buffalo mozzarella (15 minutes)
Step 6. Research local wood-fired oven temperatures (30 minutes)
Step 7. Source organic heirloom tomatoes from the market (2 hours)
Step 8. Interview local Italian chefs for advice (3 hours)
Step 9. Knead the dough by hand (20 minutes)
Step 10. Visit a specialty flour importer (4 hours)
Step 11. Design the presentation plate (1 hour)
Step 12. Finely chop fresh basil leaves (10 minutes)
Step 13. Pre-bake the crust for a blind tasting (15 minutes)
Step 14. Conduct a flavor profile test (30 minutes)
Step 15. Sharpen the pizza cutting wheel (10 minutes)
Step 16. Photograph the finished pizza for the judges (45 minutes)
Step 17. Read the contest rules and regulations (20 minutes)
Step 18. Purchase a high-quality pizza stone (1 hour)
Step 19. Simmer the sauce with fresh herbs (45 minutes)
Step 20. Clean the prep station thoroughly (30 minutes)
Step 21. Buy bulk quantities of sea salt (1 hour)
Step 22. Calibrate the oven thermometer (15 minutes)
Step 23. Record a promotional video for the contest (2 hours)
Step 24. Roast the garlic for the topping (40 minutes)
Step 25. Preheat the pizza stone in the oven (1 hour)
Step 26. Hire a professional food stylist (3 days)
Step 27. Filter the water for the dough (5 minutes)
Step 28. Practice the "toss" technique (2 hours)
Step 29. Cold-ferment the dough in the fridge (48 hours)
Step 30. Harvest wild oregano from the garden (20 minutes)
Step 31. Create a social media post about the contest (15 minutes)
Step 32. Measure out the yeast exactly (5 minutes)
Step 33. Season the new pizza stone (2 hours)
Step 34. Grate the aged parmesan cheese (10 minutes)
Step 35. Bake the competition pizza (8 minutes)
Step 36. Let the pizza rest before slicing (5 minutes)
Step 37. Submit the initial registration email (10 minutes)
Step 38. Draft the secret recipe notes (1 hour)
Step 39. Finalize the dough hydration ratio (30 minutes)
Step 40. Wash the fresh produce (15 minutes)
Step 41. Infuse olive oil with chili flakes (12 hours)
Step 42. Garnish with a drizzle of balsamic glaze (2 minutes)
Step 43. Activate the dry yeast in warm water (10 minutes)
Step 44. Browse gourmet food catalogs (2 hours)
Step 45. Arrange the toppings symmetrically (5 minutes)
Step 46. Wipe down the serving tray (5 minutes)
Step 47. Purchase a new apron (30 minutes)
Step 48. Sift the double-zero flour (10 minutes)
Step 49. Whisk the sauce to a smooth consistency (5 minutes)
Step 50. Prepare a side salad for the judges (20 minutes)
Step 51. Taste the sauce for acidity (2 minutes)
Step 52. Oil the proofing bowls (5 minutes)
Step 53. Sanitize all mixing equipment (30 minutes)
Step 54. Upload the entry video to the website (1 hour)
Step 55. Check the contest deadline (5 minutes)
Step 56. Receive the official contestant number (1 day)
Step 57. Set up the lighting for the food shoot (1 hour)
Step 58. Roll out the dough balls (15 minutes)
Step 59. Invite friends for a mock-judging session (4 hours)
Step 60. Select the best wood for the fire (1 hour)
